newsitem.title: CHINA: Kerry seeks tenants for air cargo centre.
newsitem.headline: Kerry seeks tenants for air cargo centre.

text.p: A marketing campaign has begun to lease space to major air freight forwarders in an air cargo warehouse centre under construction in Hong Kong, Ronnie Shing, director and group general manager of Kerry Godown Holdings Ltd told Reuters.

The 2.4 million square feet warehouse centre would allow freight consolidation to take place before being moved to the new airport at Chek Lap Kok(CLK), due to open in April 1998. That would reduce the number of truck journeys and costs involved with moving freight, industry source said.
Increased costs at CLK, such as bridge tolls and transport charges compared to existing charges at Kai Tak, are a major concern for many freight forwarders, they added.
"We have not yet signed up any firms, but the response has been quite encouraging," Shing said.
A wholly-owned subsidiary of Kerry Properties Ltd, the HK$1.2 billion Kerry Cargo centre is Kerry Properties' largest single investment in its Hong Kong warehousing business interests.
The 20-storey centre in Kwai Chung, expected to be completed late next year, is about 35 minutes drive from CLK and will be one of the largest developments of its type here, Shing said.
Initial marketing is aimed at attracting big name clients among Hong Kong's air freight forwarding community offering state of the art consolidation, logistics and storage facilities, Shing said.
Rentals will be HK$15 per sq ft, which is the same as the HK$2 billion Air Freight Forwarding Centre being built at the new airport, Shing said.
Shing said freight forwarders are adopting a "wait-and-see" attitude before committing to the off-airport site.

"The rental price has not initially been very attractive to them. Lowering our rental price all depends on how leasing goes, but there is still a long way to go before the centre opens. People want to see what the actual building looks like before signing up," Shing added.
Kerry Properties Ltd said it is a market leader in dry cargo, dutiable products and dangerous goods warehousing, with other interests in cold storage. But this is its first venture into air cargo.
